back_translation: For the LORD will have compassion on Jacob and will again choose Israel, and will settle them firmly in their own land. Foreigners will come join them and unite themselves with the house of Jacob.

The nations will receive them and bring them to their own place, and the house of Israel will possess those nations as male and female slaves in the land of the LORD. They will take captive those who once took them captive, and will rule over those who once oppressed them.
On the day the LORD gives you rest from your pain and torment, and from the harsh labor you were forced to perform,
you will lift up this taunt-poem against the king of Babylon: How the oppressor has come to his end! His raging fury has ceased!
The LORD has broken the club of the wicked — the scepter of the rulers,
which struck the peoples in wrath with unceasing blows, which subdued the nations in anger with unrestrained persecution.
Now the whole earth rests quietly and is still; they burst out singing with joy.
Even the juniper pines rejoice over you, and the cedars of Lebanon say: "Since you were laid low, no woodcutter has come up to cut us down."

The realm of the dead below is stirred up because of you, to welcome you when you arrive. It rouses the spirits of the dead for you — all who were leaders of the earth. It makes all who were kings of the nations rise from their thrones.
They will all say to you: "Have you too become weak like us? Have you become like us!"
Your pomp has been brought down to the realm of the dead, together with the sound of your harps. Beneath you maggots are spread as a bed, and worms are your covering.
O morning star, son of the dawn — how you have fallen from heaven! You who once laid the nations flat — you have been hewn down to the ground!
You once said in your heart: "I will ascend to the heavens; I will set my throne above the stars of God; I will sit on the mount of assembly, in the utmost reaches of the north.
I will ascend above the tops of the clouds; I will make myself like the Most High."
But you are brought down to the realm of the dead, to the deepest bottom of the pit.
Those who see you will stare at you; they consider you: "Is this the man who made the earth quake, who shook kingdoms,
who made the world like a wilderness, who destroyed its cities, who never released his captives to go home?"
All the kings of the nations lie in honor, each in his own royal resting place.
But you are flung out of your tomb like a despised branch, covered over by the slain pierced through with the sword, who are thrown down to the stones of the pit — like a corpse trampled underfoot.
You will not be joined with them in burial, because you destroyed your own land and slaughtered your own people. May the offspring of evildoers never be mentioned again forever!
Prepare a place of slaughter for his sons because of the iniquity of their fathers, so that they may not rise up and possess the land and fill the face of the world with cities again.
The LORD of Hosts declares: "I will rise up against them, and I will cut off from Babylon name and remnant, offspring and descendant," — thus the LORD has spoken.
"I will make her a haunt for owls and a stagnant marshland; I will sweep her away with the broom of destruction," — thus the LORD of Hosts has spoken.
The LORD of Hosts has sworn: "Surely, as I have conceived it, so it will be; and as I have purposed, so it will stand:
I will break Assyria in My land, and I will trample him on My mountains. Then his yoke will slip off My people, and his burden will be removed from their shoulder."
This is the plan determined for the whole earth, and this is the hand stretched out over all the nations.
For the LORD of Hosts has purposed — who can overturn it? His hand is stretched out — who can turn it back?
In the year that King Ahaz died, this burden-oracle came:
Do not rejoice, all you Philistia, that the rod which struck you is broken; for from the root of the snake a venomous viper will sprout, and its fruit will be a flying burning-serpent.
The firstborn of the destitute will have pasture to graze, and the needy will lie down in safety; but I will kill your root with famine, and it will slay your remnant.
Wail, O gate! Cry out, O city! Melt away in fear, all you Philistia! For a column of smoke is coming from the north, and there is no straggler in its ranks.
What answer, then, will be given to the envoys of that nation? This: "The LORD has founded Zion, and the afflicted of His people will take refuge in her."
